root_cause: The navigation controller sets aria-activedescendant to the list item's dataset.value (the label) instead of the element's id, causing the attribute to reference the wrong object and failing the test's expectation.
repair_strategy: Update the navigation controller to assign the list item's id attribute to aria-activedescendant, matching the expected autoCompleteJS_result_* identifiers used by the test suite.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will correctly update aria-activedescendant to reference the active option element, enabling screen readers to announce the highlighted suggestion as intended.
functional_risks: If any other code depended on aria-activedescendant containing the item's label, it would now receive the id instead; however, only this controller sets the attribute and the item's id is stable.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant equals 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
A second ArrowDown updates aria-activedescendant to 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
ArrowUp navigates backward through the list correctly.
Pressing Enter on a highlighted option fills the input with that option's label and submits the form.
